extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, their attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (practitioners in patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for preparing and filing amendments to patent specifications, claims, and drawings (including preliminary amendments and amendments in reexamination), and how examiners will treat non‑compliant or non‑responsive amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean form requirement for replacement/added paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement or added paragraph(s) must be in clean form (must not include any markings to indicate the changes that have been made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1)(ii) requires the replacement/added paragraph(s) to be in clean form. A separate marked up version must accompany the amendment to assist the examiner (see next criterion). Do not include marking in the clean version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate marked-up version for replacement paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate version of the replacement paragraph(s) that includes markings to show the changes relative to the previous version must accompany the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1)(iii). The marked-up version is an aid to the examiner. A marked-up version is not required for added paragraphs or deleted paragraphs; it is sufficient merely to indicate or identify any paragraph that has been added or deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sections and substitute specification format
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment by replacement sections or by submitting a substitute specification must be provided in clean form without markings and must be accompanied by a separate marked-up version showing changes relative to the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.77(b), 1.154(b), 1.163(c) for replacement sections and 37 CFR 1.125(b) for substitute specifications. The clean form must not show markings; a marked-up version must be supplied separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of deleted subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Any subject matter deleted by amendment can only be reinstated by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously deleted subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direction by applicant to remove a previously entered amendment will not be permitted. A canceled claim can be reinstated only by presenting it as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be rewritten when amended
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to a claim must be presented in the form of a rewritten claim; rewriting is construed as cancellation of the previous version of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Byers; any rewritten or newly added claim must be submitted in clean form. Rewriting a claim with the same number is considered cancellation of the previous claim and replacement by the new text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up requirement when rewriting a claim with the same number
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is amended by rewriting the claim with the same number, the amendment must be accompanied by a marked-up version separate from the amendment using applicant’s choice of marking system to indicate the changes being made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A parenthetical expression indicating status (e.g., 'amended', 'new') should follow the claim number in both the clean and the marked-up version. A marked-up version is not required for added claims or canceled claims, but if supplied should identify any added or canceled claims (e.g., 'Claim 6 has been canceled').

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical status of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: After each claim number the status must be indicated in a parenthetical expression (e.g., (original), (currently amended), (previously amended), (canceled), (withdrawn), (new), etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting claims (especially under the revised format), list the status with each claim. The status list provided in the guideline should be used verbatim when applicable. In a clean set, parentheticals from prior claims should not appear unless the claim is being amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of pending claims into a single clean set
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit a clean version of all pending claims in one amendment paper, consolidating previous versions for patent printing and file clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a consolidated clean set is beneficial. In the consolidated clean set, parenthetical expressions from prior versions should not appear except when a claim is being amended. Submission of a clean set of all pending claims is construed as directing cancellation of all previous versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended amendment paper organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment paper should include, in order: (A) a clean version of the amended (replacement) paragraph(s)/claim(s); (B) a remarks section (beginning on a separate sheet); and (C) a marked-up version (also beginning on a separate sheet) showing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommended format facilitates office processing. Each of these parts should begin on a separate sheet to aid indexing and electronic scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of submitting clean version without marked-up version
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim presented in clean version will constitute an assertion that it has not been modified relative to the immediate prior version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is merely presenting all pending claims in clean form without underlining/bracketing, do not submit a marked-up version. A marked-up version is needed only for claims being changed by the current amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner amendments authority (1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office is permitted to make amendments to the specification, including the claims, by examiner’s amendments without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions or deletions may be made by instructions to make the change at a precise location in the specification or the claims. See MPEP § 1302.04 for examiner amendment practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start each amendment section on separate sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section of an amendment (Introductory Comments, Amendments to the Specification, Amendments to the Claims, Remarks) must begin on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates separate indexing and electronic scanning for placement in an electronic file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of two-version requirement under revised format
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to provide two versions (a clean version and a marked-up version) of each replacement paragraph/section/substitute specification or claim is waived where an amendment is submitted in the revised format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the revised amendment format (effective Jan 31, 2003), applicants need not provide both versions when following the specified format. Exceptions apply for reissue applications and reexaminations per 37 CFR 1.173 and 1.530(d)-(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete listing of all claims when any claim is amended (revised format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment document that includes a change to an existing claim, or submission of a new claim, must include a complete listing of all claims in the application with status annotations; the listing replaces all prior versions of the claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text of each claim under examination (with markings to show current changes) must be presented. Canceled and withdrawn claims should be indicated by only the claim number and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for currently amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims being currently amended must be presented with markings to indicate changes relative to the immediate prior version: strikethrough for deleted matter and underlining for added matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the revised format, an accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented for currently amended claims. Only claims of status 'currently amended' will include markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of pending claims not amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of pending claims not being amended must be presented in clean version (without markings); any claim presented in clean version is an assertion it has not been changed relative to the immediate prior version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep claims not being amended free of markings. This distinction between marked-up amended claims and clean unamended claims is important to avoid misunderstandings about which claims changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cancellation and new claim notation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be canceled by merely providing an instruction to cancel; any claims added by amendment must be indicated as (new) and must not be underlined; all claims in each amendment paper must be presented in ascending numerical order; consecutive canceled or withdrawn claims may be aggregated in a single statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., 'Claims 1–5 (canceled)'. Follow numeric order for clarity and to conform to processing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments must be marked up (revised format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification are to be made by presenting a replacement paragraph, section, or substitute specification marked up to show changes made relative to the immediate prior version (strikethrough/underlining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accompanying clean version is not required and should not be presented under the revised format. Use strikethrough for deletions and underlining for additions to clearly show changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing changes must be made by presenting replacement figures that incorporate proposed changes and comply with 37 CFR 1.84; an explanation of the changes must be presented in the remarks section of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawing changes are not approved by the examiner, applicant will be notified in the next Office action. Any replacement drawing sheet should include all figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even though only one figure may be amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and limitations for amendments in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In reexamination proceedings, specific timing rules apply: patent owners may amend at time of request per 37 CFR 1.510(e); no amendment can be filed between the date of the request and the order for reexamination; after the order and prior to the examination phase an amendment may be filed only with the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b); during the examination phase an amendment may be filed after the first examination (37 CFR 1.112), after final/appeal if meeting 1.116 criteria, or when required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.12 and §§ 2250/2266 for reexamination amendment practice. Reexamination amendments are subject to their own specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and authority requirement for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application; unsigned or improperly signed amendments will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 1.33(b), signatures must be from: (1) a registered attorney or agent of record; (2) a registered attorney or agent not of record who acts in representative capacity under 1.34(a); (3) an assignee as provided under 3.71(b); or (4) all applicants unless assignee of entire interest has acted. Unsigned or improperly signed amendments are listed but not entered and applicant is notified to ratify within one month (see form paragraph 7.84.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unsigned or improperly signed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsigned or improperly signed amendments are not entered; the amendment will be listed on the file wrapper and the applicant will be notified to furnish a duplicate amendment properly signed or to ratify the amendment already filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant normally given a one-month time period to ratify (37 CFR 1.135(c)). Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Problems may sometimes be resolved by contacting the local representative. Amendments signed by persons removed from the register will be submitted to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment definition and entry/disapproval criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is an amendment received on or before the mail date of the first Office action; such preliminary amendments will be entered unless disapproved by the Commissioner if they unduly interfere with preparation of the first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for disapproval: state of preparation of first Office action at date of receipt and nature of any changes that would result. Preliminary amendments will not be disapproved if filed no later than three months from filing date for certain application types (see 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2)). Preliminary amendments not filed with the original application generally do not enjoy status as part of the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be fully responsive (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the applicant must reply and the reply must: be reduced to writing; distinctly and specifically point out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action; reply to every ground of objection and rejection; present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references; and appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without pointing out how the claims distinguish from the references does not comply. When amending in reply, clearly point out the patentable novelty and how amendments avoid references or objections. Formal defects and whether they touch merits may require insistence on compliance prior to indicating allowable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may accept an amendment as adequate to avoid abandonment, notify applicant to complete the reply within the remaining period for reply, or set a new time period for the applicant to complete the reply depending on bona fides, time remaining, and nature of the deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (post-March 1, 2001 rule revisions), the Office will send a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment and provide a time limit (30 days or one month) to comply. Failure to timely reply may lead to abandonment. Minor deficiencies may be acted upon; serious deficiencies (e.g., unsigned or not filed in reply) may prompt issuance of a new Office action or a one‑month period under 37 CFR 1.135(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.135(c) practice for inadvertent omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant’s reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but inadvertently omits some matter, the applicant may be given a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to supply the omission (example: minor omissions), subject to examiner discretion and time remaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice does not apply to deliberate omissions (e.g., withholding an election of species because applicant believes it improper). Once inadvertence is brought to applicant’s attention, the examiner cannot treat it as inadvertent thereafter. Examiner may refuse to grant additional time if abuse suspected. The practice does not apply after a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final Office action — limited entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after a final Office action are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply to a final Office action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, an examiner may request authorization for an examiner’s amendment to correct omissions; the date of reply is then the date of such authorization. Examiner has discretion to withdraw finality and issue a new action where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee informality and form paragraphs for non-responsive replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Informalities as to fees for additional claims are handled by technical support staff via form PTOL-319; use form paragraphs 7.95 and optionally 7.95.01 where a bona fide reply is not fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.95 gives applicant a one‑month period (or 30 days) to supply omissions in a bona fide but non-responsive reply; 7.95.01 reminds applicant to submit substantive arguments under 'Remarks' addressing applied references and distinctions.
